text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When developers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplicate lines, and give variables clearer names. This helps reduce technical debt, which builds up over time when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs. Instead, it makes the code simpler and safer to work with in the future. Teams often refactor regularly so their projects stay healthy and easy to maintain.
